name: RTX 5080: Qwen3 32B Q4_K_M decode tokens/sec
unit: tok/s - UNSOURCED, DO NOT CITE. Decommissioned 2026-10-04 (bq-): no cited source contains a decode-throughput measurement for this part and no run was performed. The number is retained only for history; the schema forbids nulling value/measured_by.
methodology: llama.cpp CUDA backend, batch size 1, 512 token prompt, 128 token output, Q4_K_M quantization, 16GB VRAM
notes:
RTX 5080 with 16GB GDDR7 at 960 GB/s. A 32B model at Q4_K_M requires ~18GB of VRAM, which exceeds the 16GB capacity. This benchmark assumes some layers offloaded to CPU. With full GPU offload, a 32B model at Q4_K_M does not fit in 16GB. The RTX 5080 is best suited for models up to ~16B at Q4_K_M.

LOAD-CONDITION AUDIT (bq- 2026-10-04) - STATUS: DECOMMISSIONED. THIS IS NOT A MEASUREMENT.
WHY THIS RECORD IS POISONOUS RATHER THAN MERELY INCOMPLETE: it looks fully condition-complete. It states batch size 1, a 512-token prompt, a 128-token output and the precision - the exact four things the repo's iron rule demands - and it is still not a benchmark. Those four values are the generic defaults shared verbatim by all 11 records in this family; they describe no run because no run happened.
WHAT THE SOURCES ACTUALLY CONTAIN: consumer-nvidia-rtx-blackwell-gpu-architecture-whitepaper (an architecture/spec document) - specification/datasheet documents containing NO decode-throughput measurement of any kind. The recorded figure (65 tok/s) appears nowhere in any cited source. Three of these notes state the reasoning explicitly as bandwidth-derived ('the N GB/s bandwidth yields ~M tokens/sec'), which is an ESTIMATE ARITHMETICALLY PROJECTED from a spec sheet, not a measurement of a model on a part.
WHY THE FIGURES ARE ALSO PHYSICALLY IMPLAUSIBLE AS SET: local-rtx-5070-13b-q4-decode records 120 tok/s on a card with 672 GB/s of bandwidth, which is faster than the same family's own 85 tok/s figure for a 1792 GB/s RTX 5090 - a 2.7x bandwidth advantage yielding a LOWER number, and 120 tok/s exceeds what any 8B 4-bit model can pull at that bandwidth.
MEASURED_BY: left as 'third_party' ONLY because schemas/benchmark.schema.json forbids null for measured_by and the audit was scoped not to edit schemas/. It is a placeholder, not a fact: nobody third-party measured this. Same for value, which is typed number and cannot be nulled here. Both should become null the moment the schema permits it; until then, status=deprecated plus this note is what stands between this record and a citation.
CONFIDENCE 0.9 -> 0.2 and reproducible true -> false: reproducible was unsupportable for a figure with no run behind it.
TO RECOVER: an actual llama.cpp or MLX-LM run on the named part, recording the engine build string, model revision, exact prompt/output token counts, whether prompts were VARIED or REPEATED (repeated prompts read 9.5-16.9x high - see ev-llamacpp-spec-bench-replay-inflates), the warmup policy, achieved clocks, and the raw tok/s counter. Until then this record must not be cited as a throughput number.
INTERCONNECT IDS FILLED 2026-10-04: interconnect_ids was empty; it now carries the interconnect list of the accelerator record(s) this run names (nvidia-rtx-5080). BASIS AND ITS LIMITS, stated because this field is easy to over-read: it records the FABRIC PRESENT IN THE HARDWARE CONFIGURATION, which is how every previously-filled record in this repo reads it, not traffic measured over that fabric. The clearest evidence for that convention is that single-GPU records already carry a scale-up fabric here - trtllm-llama31-8b-fp8-h100-1k1k-tps is 1x H100 at TP=1 and carries ['nvlink-4','nvswitch-4'] - and that host-link-only records carry a PCIe value (arc-pro-b70-mlperf-v6-1-llama2-70b-offline-tokens carries ['pcie-gen5'] on 4x Arc Pro B70, which has no GPU-to-GPU fabric at all). So a value here does NOT mean the interconnect was exercised by this particular workload, and must not be cited as evidence that it was. Whether the run actually crossed that fabric is a question about TP/EP/PP size, which this repo records in methodology, not here. NOT INVENTED: nothing was filled where the accelerator record itself carries no interconnect, so this field stays empty for any part whose own record has none - which is the honest state for a single-socket Apple sOC and for parts whose vendor publishes no host interface.
